question: to the Commission Arkadiusz Mularczyk (ECR) Subject:

The Register of Damage Caused by the Aggression of the Russian Federation against Ukraine has already received over 180 000 claims, of which approximately 58 000 have been formally registered. Nine further categories of damage have been opened, bringing the total to 21 categories. The Convention establishing an International Claims Commission for Ukraine has been signed by 40 entities; however, 25 ratifications are required for it to enter into force. To date, seven states and the European Union have ratified the convention. At the same time, 36 states and the EU have declared their readiness to participate in the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine. Europe is therefore creating a comprehensive framework encompassing a register of damages, a commission to determine claims, a source of funding and criminal liability for leaders. This also sets an important precedent for the wider debate on reparations and the enforcement of state accountability. 1.

What is the anticipated timetable for the launch of the International Claims Commission for Ukraine, and what specific measures does the Commission intend to take to secure the 17 additional ratifications of the Convention required for it to enter into force?

How does the Commission plan to make use of frozen Russian assets to finance compensation payments under the international compensation mechanism, taking into account the scale of registered claims and the categories of damages covered?

What steps does the Commission intend to take to ensure the effective functioning of the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine, supported by 36 states and the EU, in particular with regard to funding, the appointment of judges and the enforcement of criminal liability of leaders regardless of the perpetrator’s consent?
